title: Identity Management Fundamentals
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 5: Identity and Access Management (IAM): Identity Management Fundamentals.

items: Provisioning — Creating accounts and granting initial access
Management — Maintaining and updating access throughout employment
Review — Periodic access review and recertification
Deprovisioning — Disabling/deleting accounts when no longer needed
Identity lifecycle must be documented and auditable

blocks.text: The identity lifecycle encompasses the entire span from account creation to deletion:

items: Enrollment/Registration — User identity verified, account created
Provisioning — Access rights assigned based on role
Active Use — User accesses resources; activity logged
Maintenance — Role changes, access updates, password resets
Review — Periodic recertification of access rights
Deprovisioning — Account disabled/deleted upon departure or role change

blocks.text: From Chapple: "Organizations use provisioning and onboarding processes when hiring employees and deprovisioning and offboarding processes when employees leave." ⚠️ Exam Trap: Deprovisioning is just as important as provisioning. Orphaned accounts (active accounts for departed employees) are a major security risk.

items: Provisioning should follow the principle of least privilege
Access based on role, department, and job function
Automated provisioning reduces errors and ensures consistency
Deprovisioning must be immediate for involuntary termination
Account disabling (not deleting) preserves audit trail
Use role templates to assign standard access for each position
Require manager approval before granting access
Document all access grants with justification
Implement automated workflows for common provisioning tasks
Disable all accounts immediately upon termination
Revoke remote access (VPN, email, cloud)
Collect physical access badges and keys
Transfer ownership of shared resources
Archive or reassign email and files
Document deprovisioning completion
IDaaS — Cloud-based identity management
Provides SSO, MFA, directory services as a service
Reduces on-premises identity infrastructure
Examples: Okta, Azure AD, AWS IAM
Must evaluate vendor security and data sovereignty
